notes: OpenCode 2.x through the service API (#2109 P5b-1). A session's lifetime ends by archive (the watcher reports the row gone: transcript_removed) and resumes by unarchive plus a prompt, which the daemon admits under the SAME ses_… id. The service never exits, so there is no new PID lifetime.

text: The API session is admitted when its first activity lands (P3, #2107): a ses_… transcript_new. Its first state is not pinned — an API session is first seen working (P4; P5a's smoke cells)
The session binds to the one running 2.x service (pid.go servicePIDFor) — there is no client process
The first prompt drives the session to working
The 2.x plugin's session.execution.succeeded ends turn 1 (recorded as the canonical Stop hook)
Archiving the session ends its lifetime: the 2.x reader no longer lists it and reports it gone (v2SessionGone → transcript_removed)
After unarchive, the next prompt's rows are activity on the SAME ses_… id — the resumed session, not a new row
The resumed session goes ready → working on the original id
The 2.x plugin's session.execution.succeeded ends turn 2 (recorded as the canonical Stop hook)
The resumed turn completes back to ready on the original id
